constraints_found.line: Eleven attempts. Every one unrolled itself on the way to the plate. I would now like to eat some made by a professional.

constraints_found.constraint: strict diet: vegetarian / no fish or meat, needs a whole section of the menu she can eat
constraints_found.line: Mina, I've already ruled places out for you. Same standard as sushi day: a whole part of the menu with no fish and no meat in it, so you can point at anything.
and cyrus, the satay incident stays a one-off. that story doesn't get a sequel, whatever sauce or dressing it turns up in

constraints_found.constraint: budget: $$ (one tier over costs a star)
constraints_found.line: my turn. the trip fund finished its job, so i'm officially a two-dollar-sign person now
could we find somewhere calm and hushed, where nobody has to shout across the table?
and in return, my one ask for the food: simple and light. nothing that's been battered and dunked in hot oil

elimination.waterfront_starboard: Peanut-miso house dressing on the vegetarian page and peanuts on the spinach: deal-breaker for Cyrus.
elimination.waterfront_gull_point: Nothing Mina can eat (eel sauce on the veg nigiri, salmon in the cucumber roll): deal-breaker.
elimination.waterfront_mooring_post: $$$, one tier over Maya's $$: safe but costs a star (2 stars max).
elimination.waterfront_ropewalk: Loud conveyor-belt room with bells and shouting: misses the quiet preference (2 stars).
elimination.waterfront_halyard: Everything is tempura/fried: misses Brooke's light-food preference (2 stars).
elimination.waterfront_cormorant: Greek, not sushi: misses Cyrus's craving (2 stars).
elimination.waterfront_spindrift: Sushi, $$, hushed, a full fish- and meat-free page with kelp-and-mushroom miso, no fryer, peanut-free per allergy-group review. Meets everything.

notes: Peanut allergy is never stated outright; it is inferred from Brooke's 'satay incident' line. Satay = peanut sauce is reasonable general knowledge, and the 'sauce or dressing' wording nicely points at Starboard's trap. Fair but relies on the player knowing satay.

Maya's 'three signs won't sink me anymore' plus 'i will bring it up at every dinner' reads as $$ budget with $$$ tolerable-but-penalised, matching the one-star rule. Slightly ambiguous wording, but the 'two-dollar-sign person' line is clear.
Each decoy fails exactly one constraint and Spindrift's reviews explicitly confirm every one, so the answer is unique once the satay clue is decoded. No contradictions found.
Cormorant's yogurt-to-tahini line hints at a dairy angle that no one in the chat raises; harmless red herring.
